questions.stem: About the skeletal axes of the pelvic limb:
options: The mechanical axis of the thigh makes an angle of 9° with the vertical
The anatomical axis of the leg makes an angle of 9° with the vertical
The angle between the femoral and leg axes is normally about 165°
The mechanical axis of the thigh runs from the centre of the femoral head to the centre of the knee
The anatomical axis of the femoral diaphysis makes an angle of 9° with the vertical
questions.explanation: Femoral diaphysis 9°, mechanical thigh axis 3°, leg axis 3°; femur–leg angle 175° = physiological genu valgum. Also false: "The anatomical axis of the leg makes an angle of 9° with the vertical"; "The angle between the femoral and leg axes is normally about 165°".

questions.stem: A child stands with the knees touching and the ankles apart (legs in X). The angle between the femoral and leg axes is:
options: More open than 175°: pathological genu varum
More open than 175°: pathological genu valgum
More closed than 175°: pathological genu valgum
Exactly 175°: physiological
More closed than 175°: pathological genu varum
questions.explanation: Legs in X = pathological genu valgum (more closed angle); legs in O = genu varum (more open angle).

questions.stem: About the hip bone (os coxae):
options: It connects the spine and the pelvic limb
It is oriented with the notched border backward and the foramen downward
It is a flat bone shaped like a two-bladed propeller
It is a long bone
It is formed by the ilium, ischium and pubis meeting in the acetabulum in a "Y"
questions.explanation: Orientation: articular cavity outward, foramen downward, notched border backward.

questions.stem: The acetabulum:
options: Its limbus has three notches, the superior one being wide and deep
Its peripheral part is the semilunar surface covered with hyaline cartilage
Is a deep spheroid excavation limited by the acetabular limbus
Its central acetabular fossa is covered with hyaline cartilage
Is entirely covered with articular cartilage
questions.explanation: Only the crescent-shaped peripheral semilunar surface is articular; the central acetabular fossa is not. Also false: "Its limbus has three notches, the superior one being wide and deep"; "Its central acetabular fossa is covered with hyaline cartilage".

questions.stem: The obturator foramen:
options: Lies below the acetabulum
Is limited above by the ischiopubic ramus
Is triangular and wide in men
Is closed by two obturator membranes
Is oval and narrow in women
questions.explanation: Above: cranial branch of the pubis with the obturator groove; below: ischiopubic ramus; in front: body of the pubis; behind: ischial tuberosity. Also false: "Is triangular and wide in men"; "Is oval and narrow in women".

questions.stem: Which of the following belong to the lateral surface of the hip bone?
options: The acetabulum
The auricular surface
The acetabular limbus
The gluteal surface with its gluteal lines
The iliac fossa
questions.explanation: Iliac fossa and auricular surface (articular with the sacrum) belong to the medial surface.

questions.stem: The medial surface of the hip bone:
options: Presents the acetabulum
Presents the anterior and posterior gluteal lines
Is crossed by the arcuate line
Presents the pecten pubis along the upper border of the obturator foramen
Presents, above the arcuate line, the gluteal surface
questions.explanation: The gluteal lines are on the gluteal surface (lateral face). Also false: "Presents, above the arcuate line, the gluteal surface"; "Presents the acetabulum".

questions.stem: The iliac crest:
options: Is the superior border of the hip bone
Is the posterior border of the hip bone
Is palpable under the skin
Is a preferred site for bone punctures and bone graft harvesting
Articulates with the opposite hip bone
questions.explanation: The inferior border's anterior segment articulates with the opposite hip bone (pubic symphysis).

questions.stem: Which structures belong to the posterior border of the hip bone?
options: The greater sciatic notch
The anterior inferior iliac spine
The ischial spine
The iliopectineal eminence
The lesser sciatic notch
questions.explanation: Posterior border: PSIS, small innominate notch, PIIS, greater sciatic notch, ischial spine, lesser sciatic notch, ischial tuberosity. AIIS and iliopectineal eminence are on the anterior border.

questions.stem: Match the angle of the hip bone with its landmark:
options: Anteroinferior angle: ischial spine
Posterosuperior angle: posterior superior iliac spine
Anterosuperior angle: anterior superior iliac spine
Anteroinferior angle: pubic spine
Posteroinferior angle: ischial tuberosity
questions.explanation: The ischial spine is on the posterior border, not an angle.

questions.stem: About the bony pelvis:
options: The superior strait is limited behind by the sacral promontory
The superior strait is limited in front by the ischial tuberosities
The superior strait divides it into anterior and posterior pelvis
The greater pelvis is also called the obstetrical pelvis
It is formed by the two hip bones, the sacrum and the coccyx
questions.explanation: In front, the superior strait is limited by the (upper border of the) pubic symphysis; laterally by the arcuate lines. Also false: "The superior strait divides it into anterior and posterior pelvis"; "The greater pelvis is also called the obstetrical pelvis".

questions.stem: About the femoral diaphysis:
options: Its anterior border is the linea aspera
The linea aspera trifurcates below, delimiting the popliteal surface
Its posterior border is the linea aspera
The linea aspera bifurcates above
Its three surfaces give insertion to the quadriceps
questions.explanation: The linea aspera is the prominent rough posterior border. Also false: "The linea aspera bifurcates above"; "The linea aspera trifurcates below, delimiting the popliteal surface".

questions.stem: The femoral head:
options: Gives attachment at the fovea to the ligament of the head of the femur
Articulates with the glenoid cavity
Represents 1/3 of a sphere
Is covered with cartilage except at the fovea capitis
Represents 2/3 of a sphere
questions.explanation: The femoral head is 2/3 of a sphere (the humeral head is 1/3) and articulates with the acetabulum.

questions.stem: The femoral neck–shaft angle of a patient measures 115°. This is:
options: Normal
Coxa vara
Genu valgum
Coxa valga
Genu varum
questions.explanation: Normal inclination is 125°–130°; a more closed angle is coxa vara, a more open one coxa valga.

questions.stem: About the trochanters of the femur:
options: They are connected posteriorly by the intertrochanteric line
They are connected anteriorly by the intertrochanteric crest
The trochanteric fossa is on the medial face of the greater trochanter
The lesser trochanter is a medial conical projection
The greater trochanter is a lateral quadrangular projection
questions.explanation: Anteriorly: intertrochanteric line; posteriorly: intertrochanteric crest.

questions.stem: About the distal epiphysis of the femur:
options: The femoral trochlea articulates with the posterior surface of the patella
The intercondylar fossa is anterior
The epicondyles give attachment to the cruciate ligaments
The intercondylar fossa gives attachment to the collateral ligaments
The femoral condyles articulate with the tibial plateau and the patella
questions.explanation: The condyles are separated posteriorly by the intercondylar fossa; the trochlea (patellar surface) is anterior. Also false: "The intercondylar fossa gives attachment to the collateral ligaments"; "The epicondyles give attachment to the cruciate ligaments".

questions.stem: The patella:
options: Its anterior surface articulates with the femoral trochlea
Its base receives the patellar ligament
Its apex receives the quadriceps tendon
Lies in the tendon of the quadriceps femoris
Is a sesamoid bone, flat and triangular
questions.explanation: The posterior surface is articular with the femoral trochlea; the anterior surface is convex. Also false: "Its base receives the patellar ligament"; "Its apex receives the quadriceps tendon".

questions.stem: About the tibial diaphysis:
options: Its medial border is the interosseous border
Its anterior surface is crossed by the soleal line
Its anterior border is the subcutaneous tibial crest
Its medial surface gives insertion to the tibialis anterior
Its lateral surface gives insertion to the tibialis anterior
questions.explanation: The lateral border of the tibia is the interosseous border. Also false: "Its medial surface gives insertion to the tibialis anterior"; "Its anterior surface is crossed by the soleal line".

questions.stem: Which structure of the tibia gives insertion to the patellar ligament?
options: The medial tibial tuberosity
The fibular notch
The intercondylar tubercles
The anterior tibial tuberosity
The medial malleolus
questions.explanation: The anterior tibial tuberosity on the anterior face of the proximal epiphysis receives the patellar ligament.

questions.stem: About the distal tibia and the fibula:
options: The tibial plafond is formed by the inferior tibial articular surface and the medial malleolar surface
The fibular notch is on the medial face of the distal tibia
The head of the fibula articulates with the tibia
The medial malleolus is longer than the lateral malleolus and descends lower
The fibula articulates with the femur
questions.explanation: The fibula articulates with the tibia above and the tibia and talus below; it does not reach the femur. Also false: "The fibular notch is on the medial face of the distal tibia"; "The medial malleolus is longer than the lateral malleolus and descends lower".

questions.stem: About the bones of the foot:
options: The anterior tarsus contains the talus and the calcaneus
The posterior tarsus is formed by the talus and the calcaneus
The two tarsal rows are joined by the Lisfranc joint
The metatarsus is joined to the tarsus by the Lisfranc joint
The foot has 28 bones
questions.explanation: The two tarsal rows are joined by the Chopart midtarsal joint; Lisfranc is the tarsometatarsal joint. Also false: "The foot has 28 bones"; "The anterior tarsus contains the talus and the calcaneus".

questions.stem: About the toes and sesamoid bones of the foot:
options: There are 14 phalanges
Two sesamoid bones are constant, opposite the head of the 1st metatarsal
Sesamoid bones of the foot are on its dorsal surface
The hallux has two phalanges
Metatarsals are numbered I to V from medial to lateral
questions.explanation: Sesamoid bones of the foot are always on the plantar surface.
